extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners admitted to practice before the USPTO (especially those facing or advising on reciprocal discipline), OED staff, and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 following a suspension by a court of competent jurisdiction; explains procedural notices, opportunity to respond, grounds for discipline, and post-discipline duties and publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may file a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting that the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by another tribunal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and Order must be mailed to the respondent (here, by certified mail). The Notice provides an opportunity to respond opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline. If no timely response is filed, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the other tribunal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to oppose under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the other tribunal, based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A respondent must timely invoke the specific grounds listed in § 11.24(d)(1) in order to oppose reciprocal discipline; failure to file a response forfeits that opportunity (as occurred here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a response, the Office may find there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and conclude that imposing reciprocal discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-response can lead the USPTO to adopt the other tribunal's findings and impose identical discipline without further factual dispute; counsel should treat the response deadline seriously to preserve arguments under § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) may be predicated upon being suspended from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, the Fourth Circuit suspended Respondent for two years for failing to represent his client with reasonable diligence and for failing to comply with repeated court orders and show-cause directives. Such state or federal suspensions can form the predicate for USPTO discipline under § 11.804(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of misconduct: failure to represent with reasonable diligence and failure to obey court orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The discipline was predicated upon a determination that Respondent 'failed to represent his client with reasonable diligence when he failed to comply with repeated orders of the Court to file a brief and appendix despite repeated notifications from the Clerk's Office; and failed to respond to the Criminal Justice Act Panel's order to show cause.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of professional responsibility (e.g., lack of diligence, failure to respond to procedural orders) and corresponding violations of local bar rules or appellate rules (here: Rule 1.3 of the Virginia State Bar Professional Guidelines and Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure 30(a) and 31(a)) are concrete examples that support suspension and/or reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of imposed discipline (practice limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Respondent is suspended from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for two years, effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies the area of USPTO practice affected (trademark and other non-patent matters) and, where applicable, notes whether the respondent is authorized to practice in patent matters (here: 'Mark Howard Allenbaugh is not authorized to practice before the Office in patent matters').

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notification requirements (Official Gazette and 37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes a sample Notice of Suspension to be published and specifies the channels and recipients for disciplinary notice required by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-discipline duties (37 C.F.R. § 11.58 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 following imposition of discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Order references § 11.58 without detailing its contents, practitioners should consult that regulation for required notifications, reporting obligations, and other duties that suspended practitioners must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and statutory basis for action
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO's authority to impose reciprocal discipline and to publish and notify others of such discipline rests on federal statute and the cited Code of Federal Regulations; citing the statutory/regulatory authority in orders is required practice.
